coverage.eligibilityUniverse: complete selected-week schedule/deep-dive slate, not weekly-board decision overlay
coverage.screenRule: Screen every FBS-vs-FBS underdog with verified moneyline +300 or longer. FCS-vs-FBS is also researched when a widely posted ML exists, but tracked separately because cross-level independent pricing is less reliable.
coverage.requiredForConsideration: For +1000 or longer, Upset Viability Score >=75 plus a credible QB/offensive path and favorite-volatility case.

candidates.qbThesis: Christopher Vizzina is inexperienced as the full-time starter but has flashed high-end passing output; Clemson retains enough surrounding talent to create a real offensive ceiling rather than requiring a purely fluky upset.
candidates.compressionThesis: Clemson's best path is defensive containment plus enough run-game improvement to avoid a high-possession track meet.
favoriteVolatility: LSU is in Year 1 under Lane Kiffin
LSU roster/QB chemistry still carries Week 1 variance
candidates.explosiveTurnoverPath: Clemson's defensive front and skill talent provide a credible pressure/explosive-play route.
candidates.expertResidual: Mixed but not disqualifying; current public analysis highlights meaningful uncertainty on both sides.
candidates.action: Full ML deep dive and live price verification before activation.

candidates.qbThesis: Tulsa needs stable QB play and enough efficiency to keep OSU from turning its talent infusion into short fields; QB edge is not yet a strength of the case.
candidates.compressionThesis: Home field and rivalry familiarity offer a plausible path to a lower-possession game if Tulsa can stay on schedule.
favoriteVolatility: only five returning players with at least four OSU starts in 2025
candidates.explosiveTurnoverPath: The thesis depends on early-season cohesion mistakes from a massively rebuilt favorite more than on a dominant Tulsa defense.
candidates.expertResidual: CONTRADICTORY: Josh Pate has Oklahoma State -13.5 as a Ramen Noodle Express best bet, citing Morris and the experienced transfer roster.
candidates.action: Priority research candidate, but expert contradiction lowers confidence and prevents consensus framing.

candidates.qbThesis: Elite-FCS program quality and offensive competence make SDSU materially different from a generic FCS underdog, though cross-level QB modeling remains lower-confidence.
candidates.compressionThesis: SDSU's strongest upset path is physical, efficient football that shortens the game and keeps Northwestern from exploiting depth.
favoriteVolatility: Northwestern is not an elite Big Ten roster
early-season system/QB uncertainty remains more relevant than conference label
candidates.explosiveTurnoverPath: SDSU can plausibly create pressure and field-position leverage without needing multiple non-offensive scores.
candidates.expertResidual: Market-model disagreement is notable: Oddschecker displayed a 21% SDSU win estimate and 56% ATS lean at +13.5.
candidates.action: Priority cross-level deep dive; do not treat FCS label as an automatic disqualifier, but keep independent-probability confidence lower.

candidates.classification: LIVE LONGSHOT / NOT BETTABLE UNDER +1000 RULE
candidates.qbThesis: Caden Pinnick arrives after FCS Freshman All-America recognition and gives WSU a credible upside variable.
candidates.compressionThesis: Rivalry dynamics and enough returning offensive pieces can keep the game competitive if WSU avoids early negative script.
candidates.explosiveTurnoverPath: Apple Cup volatility plus a new QB with mobility/upside provides an asymmetric path.
candidates.expertResidual: No strong independent confirmation currently overcomes the large underlying talent gap.
candidates.action: Monitor only; score is below the mandatory 75 threshold for +1000-or-longer consideration.

candidates.qbThesis: Boise has program competence but no verified QB advantage over Oregon.
candidates.compressionThesis: A strong rushing identity can shorten the game, but Oregon's front and depth materially reduce that path.
candidates.explosiveTurnoverPath: Boise would need unusually strong field-position/turnover variance.
candidates.expertResidual: Blue Chip Analytics makes Oregon -27.6 versus a market around -24, a material anti-Boise signal.
candidates.action: Research watch only; large payout is not enough to offset an independent model that is stronger on Oregon than the market.

candidates.qbThesis: Ohio is rebuilding and lacks a verified QB mismatch in its favor.
candidates.compressionThesis: The total around 46.5 materially helps the underdog path by reducing expected possessions and scoring opportunities.
favoriteVolatility: Week 1 only; Nebraska has more continuity than the strongest Lab targets
candidates.explosiveTurnoverPath: Ohio needs defensive/field-position variance rather than a pure talent win.
candidates.expertResidual: Some external win-probability outputs imply more upset chance than the moneyline, but confidence is limited by roster transition.

candidates.qbThesis: Caden Veltkamp returns after leading the nation's No. 1 passing offense by yards per game in 2025, giving FAU a legitimate high-variance offensive weapon.
candidates.compressionThesis: This is not a natural compression profile; FAU's path is more likely explosive scoring variance.
favoriteVolatility: Florida is starting Aaron Philo in Week 1
candidates.explosiveTurnoverPath: FAU's passing volume creates a credible explosive-play path that many +1600 dogs lack.
candidates.expertResidual: numberFire displayed Florida at 94.6% win probability, close to the market break-even and not a strong independent value signal.
candidates.action: Interesting archetype-learning game, but current score does not clear +1000 threshold.

candidates.qbThesis: Braden Atkinson brings FCS success but enters an overhauled offense.
candidates.compressionThesis: Some upset script exists from last year's close game, but Houston's continuity is the stronger structural signal.
favoriteVolatility: limited; Houston returns head coach, all coordinators, QB Conner Weigman and major contributors
candidates.explosiveTurnoverPath: Requires more variance than the current matchup evidence supports.
candidates.expertResidual: BetMGM simulation showed Houston 98.4%; numberFire 93.5%. Both are anti-Oregon State relative to the ML.

candidates.qbThesis: Broc Lowry is a dual-threat QB and gives Western a coherent rushing/option-style variance path.
candidates.compressionThesis: Western returns a run-first identity after a 10-4 MAC-title season; shortening the game is its clearest route.
favoriteVolatility: limited; Michigan remains the materially stronger roster
candidates.explosiveTurnoverPath: Western's 2025 defense ranked top-10 nationally in scoring defense and top-5 in sacks, creating some pressure-based upset mechanism.
candidates.expertResidual: Michigan Football Focus projects Michigan 95.6%, while numberFire displayed 89.9%; disagreement is too wide to treat the optimistic tail as a clean value signal.
candidates.action: High-interest learning game, but 64 is below the mandatory 75 threshold for a +2000 candidate.

learningMarkers.governance: Use only as a prospective feature-learning observation. Do not reconstruct a pregame UMass score from in-game or final-result facts.
